title: Multiply a decimal by a whole number (0.125 × 3) with models and estimation

lesson.title: Three Scoops of Trail Mix: 0.125 x 3

steps.say: You already know that one hundred twenty-five times three is three hundred seventy-five, and you know that zero point one two five means one hundred twenty-five thousandths. Today we put those two things together, because at the store one scoop of trail mix weighs zero point one two five kilograms, and Grandma wants three scoops.

visual.caption: 0.125 is 1 tenth, 2 hundredths, 5 thousandths — 125 thousandths in all

steps.say: Before we calculate, let us guess smartly. Zero point one two five is just a little more than one tenth. Three jumps of one tenth land on three tenths. So our answer should be a little more than zero point three — and definitely less than one whole kilogram.

visual.caption: Three jumps of about one tenth land near three tenths

steps.say: Now let us build zero point one two five with base ten blocks. For this lesson the big flat is one tenth, the rod is one hundredth, and the tiny cube is one thousandth. So one scoop is one flat, two rods, and five cubes — one hundred twenty-five thousandths.

Three scoops means three copies of those blocks. Three flats, six rods, and fifteen cubes. Ten of those cubes trade up for one rod, so we get three flats, seven rods, and five cubes — three hundred seventy-five thousandths, which we write as zero point three seven five kilograms. Look, it matches our guess of a little more than three tenths.

Here is the quick way, and here is the trap. Multiply as if there were no dot: one hundred twenty-five times three is three hundred seventy-five. Then count the decimal places in zero point one two five — there are three of them, so the answer needs three decimal places too, giving zero point three seven five. Some kids just line the dot up under the dot and write three point seven five. But three point seven five kilograms is almost four kilograms of trail mix from three little scoops. Way off! Always count the places, then check against your estimate.

visual.caption: 0.375 is correct; 3.75 is nowhere near our estimate

steps.say: And one more thing to remember: multiplying does not always make a number bigger. If you buy zero point five of a kilogram eight times, that is only four kilograms, which is smaller than eight. So let your estimate be the boss, every single time.

lesson.answer: Multiply like whole numbers, then count the decimal places in the decimal factor and give the answer the same number of places: 0.125 x 3 = 0.375.

practice.question: A craft store sells ribbon in pieces that are 0.132 metres long. Rani buys 3 pieces for her science fair board. In your notebook, draw base ten blocks for one piece, where a flat is one tenth, a rod is one hundredth, and a small cube is one thousandth — so one piece is 1 flat, 3 rods, and 2 cubes. Now draw three of those groups. First estimate the total, then find the exact total length in metres.
practice.answer: Estimate: 0.132 is about one tenth, and three tenths is 0.3, so the answer is a bit more than 0.3 metres. Exact: three groups give 3 flats, 9 rods, and 6 cubes, which is 396 thousandths. Since 132 times 3 is 396, and 0.132 has three decimal places, the answer is 0.396 metres.
